variations: One-dog mode: one strip, with an easy way around the towel.
Seated version: tape the strip near your chair and wait for the dog to come.
Puppy or hesitant dog: use a barely damp cloth and a short strip.
No-paper version: damp towel then a plain dark tile or bath mat.
substitutes: Black trash bags cut open instead of craft paper, taped down flat
title: The Vanishing Prints
clue: A strip of dark paper holds a secret that only lasts a minute or two.
reveal: Your dog walks, when they like, over a damp towel and then a strip of dark paper. Prints appear and fade as they dry, so there is a short window to photograph them. With two dogs, each takes a turn alone.
objective: Let your dog leave a line of damp prints on dark paper, photograph them while they last, and, with two dogs, compare both sets.
instructions: Tape a strip of dark craft paper on a non-slip floor. Lay a folded damp (not dripping) towel at the start. With two dogs, the other dog waits behind a closed door in another room with a toy.
Put a mat with a toy and water at the far end so your dog has somewhere nice to arrive.
Bring dog A in on leash or loose and stand at the far end with a toy. Let them walk across the towel and paper at their own pace. Do not push or coax a reluctant dog; a route around is fine.
Prints show as darker marks, then fade. As soon as your dog steps off, photograph the strip while it is wet.
Dry their paws on a clean towel and let them rest. With two dogs, move dog A out of sight, lay fresh paper, then bring in dog B for their own strip.
When both dogs are done, bring the photos together on a phone and compare: whose are bigger, who walked straighter, who left the most prints.
Optional: write the dog's name and the date beside the strip as it dries to keep a faded print.
twist: The art disappears: the prints show up for a minute or two while the paper is wet, so you have a short window to photograph the tracks.
completion: Each dog has left at least one print or chosen not to, and the photo is taken.
photoIdea: The finished strip with prints, shot top-down within a minute of the walk, with the dog's paw at the edge.
memoryPrompt: Whose prints were bigger, and who took the straighter line?
supplies: Dark craft paper or poster board
safety: Check the floor under the paper is non-slip and wipe up drips; never tape paper over stairs.
One dog at a time; the other stays out of sight behind a closed door, and no toys or bowls are shared.
Dry their paws after, and skip the walk if a dog avoids wet surfaces.
